Chronic heavy metal exposure drives mitochondrial remodeling and metabolic reprogramming to enhance sperm velocity in wild tree sparrows
Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
articles.abstract: Abstract Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

articles.title: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
articles.abstract: Abstract How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo.

articles.title: Laminated structure design accommodates thermal expansion mismatch for mechanically and thermally dual-stable thermoelectric contacts
A genetic platform to deconvolve efficacy and toxicity reveals the on-target effects of CDK11 inhibition in vivo
Superradiant charge density waves in a driven hybrid cavity-matter system
articles.abstract: Abstract Optical cavities enable strong, long-range, light-matter interactions that drive collective ordering, such as superradiant self-organization in ultracold atomic gases. Extending these ideas to solid-state electron systems could enable continuous-wave optical control of electronic order, but is impeded by the mismatch between optical wavelengths and electronic length scales. Here, we propose a platform for realizing superradiant charge density waves in doped, driven transition-metal dichalcogenides coupled to an optical cavity. A nanoscale grating generates electric fields at large in-plane optical momenta, allowing cavity photons to couple efficiently to electronic density fluctuations through exciton-polaron processes. Using a linear-stability analysis, we determine the threshold for superradiant ordering and map out the driven phase diagram. We show that matching the grating periodicity to the enhanced electronic density fluctuations—such as those near Wigner crystallization—lowers the required pump intensity. Our results establish a route toward cavity-controlled electronic order in quantum materials.

articles.title: Spatially resolved host and microbiota RNA profiling in the mouse gut using microDBiT
Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB
Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
The 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a far more extreme event
articles.abstract: Abstract In 2023, the North Atlantic Ocean experienced a marine heatwave of unprecedented intensity and duration, raising the question of whether substantially more severe outcomes were physically plausible under comparable present-day preconditioning, and which processes could produce them. Here, we apply ensemble boosting to a coupled Earth system model to generate physically consistent alternative evolutions of a 2023-like event. The boosted ensemble produced marine heatwaves lasting up to 579 days, reaching maximum intensities of 4.5 °C above climatology and cumulative intensities of 717 °C·days, compared with 240 days, 2.9 °C and 224 °C·days in observations. Detailed analyses of the longest and most intense events highlight contrasting roles for persistent Euro-Atlantic high pressure, reduced turbulent heat loss, enhanced shortwave radiation and upper-ocean heat redistribution. Finally, we place these present-day storylines in the context of future warming, showing that events comparable to the observed 2023 event become increasingly common as global warming progresses.

articles.title: Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization
articles.abstract: Abstract Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315–579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9–20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9–35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO 2 emissions by 94.3–258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization.

articles.title: Resolving short-term meteorological variability amplifies projected glacier loss and sea-level rise
articles.abstract: Abstract Global glacier models typically rely on temperature-index mass balance calculations forced with aggregated meteorological data, limiting their ability to resolve short-term variability. Here, we develop a daily-resolution version of the Global Glacier Evolution Model (GloGEM), which we apply globally and compare against the monthly configuration. Our results show that the daily model more closely reproduces mass balance observations and provides a more detailed representation of glacier runoff. Accounting for short-term meteorological variability leads to systematically greater projected mass loss, with up to 25% greater loss in Svalbard. These differences arise from extreme melt days, precipitation-phase transitions, and surface-type feedbacks not fully represented at monthly resolution. Globally, the daily model yields ice volume losses of 26 ± 10% under low-emission and 47 ± 17% under high-emission scenarios over 2025-2100 (ensemble mean ± 1 StD), resulting in an additional 5-10% mass loss (20-33 mm of global mean sea-level rise) relative to the monthly implementation. Resolving high-frequency forcing, or accounting for its effects through parameterisations, is therefore essential for robust glacier projections, while its omission may systematically underestimate future glacier loss.

articles.title: Controlling the shell growth mechanism and interfacial oxidation of InAs/ZnSe quantum dots for shortwave infrared emission
articles.abstract: Abstract Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Furthermore, integrating CQDs into LEDs often introduces severe interfacial quenching and intrinsic charge imbalances. Here we report a highly efficient heavy-metal-free SWIR LED operating at 1525 nm, enabled by tailored injection strategies and oxidation-induced interfacial engineering. Optimized high-temperature ZnCl₂ treatment and continuous precursor injection improve shell nucleation and growth, while controlled interfacial oxidation is associated with reduced shell-thickness-dependent strain signatures and improved PLQY retention during shell thickening. Together, these strategies yield measured PLQYs exceeding 55% for emission beyond 1400 nm. Moreover, we demonstrate that incorporating a semiconducting InAs CQD interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial quenching and regulates electron over-injection. Combined with a doped hole-transport layer to reduce series resistance, our optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 3.5% and a record radiance of ~17 W sr −1 m −2 , alongside a T50 operational lifetime of 16 h. Our findings suggest that integrating mechanism-driven shell growth with rational device engineering offers a strategy to overcome current bottlenecks in colloidal emitters, facilitating the transition toward short-wave infrared applications.

articles.title: Nano-kinetic implant surface mediates osteo-antibacterial synergy through electromagnetic-mechanical coupling
Plasma eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 as T2 biomarkers for biological staging and prognosis in Alzheimer’s disease
articles.abstract: Abstract Plasma biomarkers that reflect distinct stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) could enable scalable biological staging. We evaluated phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species across multiple analytical platforms and the endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region containing residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) using a dedicated LC-MS/MS platform in a well-characterized cohort with amyloid PET and a subset with tau PET. While T1 biomarkers increased during preclinical stages, eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 increased later, consistent with fibrillar tau aggregation. eMTBR-tau243 showed the strongest and stage-dependent associations with regional tau PET and cognition, outperforming T1 biomarkers in predicting cross-sectional and longitudinal cognition. A plasma-based tau staging system integrating p-tau217 and eMTBR-tau243 closely aligned with PET-based tau staging and predicted longitudinal cognitive trajectories. These findings support plasma eMTBR-tau243 as a prototypical T2 biomarker and highlight the potential of plasma-based tau staging for prognosis and therapeutic decision-making in AD.

articles.title: Ten protein panel predicts ALS from plasma with high accuracy
Near-infrared-responsive thia-hexaphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks for cancer phototherapy
articles.abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COF) have emerged as promising phototherapeutic platforms for tumor therapy, where the columnar π-arrayed metal-free photosensitizers serve as both a cooperative light-harvesting antenna and a semiconducting scaffold for efficient charge-carrier separation and transport. However, the phototherapeutic agents based on COFs are usually activated with ultraviolet and visible light, resulting in the limitation of deep-tissue phototherapy. Herein, we develop near-infrared-responsive COFs through elaborate design and synthesis of a thia-hexaphyrin building block, which feature well-aligned conjugation skeletons for the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and photothermal effect upon 808 nm laser irradiation, outperforming conventional porphyrin-based COFs. This porous framework exhibits high phototherapeutic efficacy, leading to the tumor suppression for 4T1 tumors and CT26 tumors in female mouse model by inducing immunogenic cell death through phototherapy and triggering systemic anti-tumor immune responses.

articles.title: Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design
articles.abstract: Abstract Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

articles.title: Passive abortive infection mechanisms targeting phage long tail fiber proteins
articles.abstract: Abstract Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies against phage infection, yet mechanisms directly targeting viral proteins remain scarcely documented. In this study, we characterize two bacterial defense systems: TFAD1 featuring a serine protease and TFAD2 featuring a Ser/Thr kinase. We show that TFAD1 and TFAD2 act on phage long tail fiber proteins via protein degradation and phosphorylation, respectively. Intriguingly, both systems allow complete phage replication cycles but generate non-infective progeny—a mechanism distinct from classical abortive infection (Abi), which we term “passive Abi”. Our findings expand the paradigm of bacterial immunity by unveiling protease- and kinase-mediated incapacitation of phage structural proteins, offering insights into the molecular arms race between bacteria and phages.

articles.title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion

Divergent Responses
of Manganese Oxides to Olivine
Dissolution and Their Control on Trace Metal Fates under an Ocean
Alkalinity Enhancement Scenario
articles.abstract: Abstract Olivine-based ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is a promising carbon dioxide removal technology; however, the geochemical fate of olivine-derived toxic metals, particularly nickel (Ni) and chromium (Cr) at marine sediment interfaces, remains poorly constrained. We employed dialysis-membrane microcosms to isolate olivine from Mn oxides, allowing only dissolved species to diffuse and react under three olivine loadings (1, 5, and 10 g L–1) in seawater for 60 days. Results revealed that (1) Ni was preferentially sequestered by the Mn oxides, with δ-MnO2 showing higher uptake capacity than birnessite, (2) Cr was co-sequestered with secondary Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxides rather than adsorbing directly onto Mn oxides, and (3) synergistic Ni2+ isomorphic substitution and Fe(II)-driven Mn(III) reduction rearranged δ-MnO2 into a more stable hexagonal layered framework. Consequently, both δ-MnO2 and birnessite act as long-term Ni sinks, preventing Ni remobilization via desorption or diagenetic phase transitions. These findings support a proposed “spatial decoupling” OAE strategy, where olivine is pre-dissolved in land- or ship-based reactors to remove Cr via Fe co-precipitation. Subsequent discharge of the Ni-bearing alkaline effluent into shallow coastal regions allows benthic Mn oxides to scavenge Ni, reducing toxicity risks associated with direct mineral contact.

articles.title: Fe3 + Activation of Metal Sulfides for High-Performance Mercury Removal from Nonferrous Smelting Gas: A Dual Mercury Adsorption Mechanism
articles.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric elemental mercury (Hg0) emitted from the nonferrous metallurgy industry poses severe risks to ecosystems. Although metal sulfides are promising in Hg0 adsorption under high-concentration SO2 conditions, they typically suffer from poor performance at elevated temperatures due to weak binding affinity. Herein, a trivalent iron (Fe3+) activation strategy to boost Hg0 adsorption activity of metal sulfides was developed for the first time, which leverages electron-deficient Fe3+ to induce electronic reconstruction. This Fe3+ activation strategy is applicable to various metal sulfides, generating Fe sites with high activity and stability. Among the various candidates, the Fe3+-activated MoS2 delivers a record-theoretical saturated Hg0 adsorption capacity of 69.56 mg·g–1 at 150 °C, which is 4.35 times higher than that of pristine MoS2. The sulfur vacancies on MoS2 serve as the key anchoring sites for Fe3+, generating stable single-atom, dimer, and trimer Fe configurations. These new Fe centers, benefiting from charge modulation, can simultaneously adsorb two Hg atoms via charge transfer and orbital hybridization. The Fe3+-activated MoS2 exhibits strong resistance to SO2 and H2O, maintaining high Hg0 removal efficiency under a smelting gas atmosphere. This work reveals new configurations of Hg adsorption and provides a convenient route to design high-performance sorbents for heavy metal purification.

articles.title:
Photochemical
Interactions
of Nitrate Photolysis and
Photosensitization of BBOA: Enhanced HONO Production and the Formation
of Nitrophenols
articles.abstract: Abstract Renoxification of nitrate to reactive nitrogen species (RNS) can sustain atmospheric oxidant production. Because nitrate and light-absorbing brown carbon can coexist in biomass burning (BB) plumes, their photochemical interaction may alter RNS cycling. Furthermore, nitration of phenols in biomass burning organic aerosol (BBOA) can form nitrophenols, potentially increasing the warming effect of aged BBOA. Yet the mechanisms of renoxification and nitration in irradiated nitrate-BBOA mixtures remain poorly understood. We experimentally investigate these coupled processes over a wide range of fir-wood BBOA concentrations during aqueous nitrate photolysis (10 mM) under acidic conditions using H2SO4. At low BBOA concentration (TOCBBOA/NO3– ≤ 0.0036 mg L–1/mg L–1), the steady-state production rate of HONO (Pss_HONO) increased as BBOA concentration increased, reaching a maximum enhancement factor of 1.8 driven primarily by triplet-mediated photosensitized reduction of NO2 to HONO. At higher BBOA concentration (TOCBBOA/NO3– > 0.0036 mg L–1/mg L–1), Pss_HONO progressively decreased and was nearly fully suppressed at TOCBBOA/NO3– = 0.7 mg L–1/mg L–1. This inhibition is attributed to reactions of aqueous HNO2/NO2 with phenols, accompanied by formation of nitrophenols. These findings point to a potentially overlooked daytime HONO source and an atmospheric source of nitrophenols, a key class of BrC chromophores, via photochemical interactions between nitrate photolysis and photosensitization of BBOA.

articles.title:
Submarine Groundwater
Discharge Acts as a Significant
Vector for Coastal Organophosphate Esters: Joint Evidence from Pollution
Surveys and Radionuclide Analysis
articles.abstract: Abstract Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are ubiquitous marine contaminants that raise global concern. While surface inputs are well-studied, the role of subsurface transport remains poorly constrained. Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) drives seawater-groundwater interactions, yet its impact on OPEs behavior remains overlooked. This study comprehensively investigates the distribution, transport property and sources of OPEs from coastal groundwater to seawater in the Beibu Gulf, China. No statistically significant difference in Σ19OPEs levels was found between groundwater and tidal flat porewater, while both matrices exhibited significantly higher levels than seawater. The high compositional similarity, strong correlations (p < 0.01) and PCA overlap of OPEs in different waters, as well as their shared source profiles indicated the transport potential of OPEs from groundwater to seawater. Multiple statistical modeling integrating OPEs, environmental factors and DOM components reveals the land-to-sea transport pathways and biogeochemical processes of OPEs via SGD. Furthermore, radon isotope analysis verified the presence of SGD, offering evidence for SGD-mediated OPE transport. For the first time, this work integrates pollutant investigation, multiple statistical analysis, and radionuclide tracing, to identify SGD as a previously underestimated vector of coastal OPEs and elucidates its potential transport mechanisms, providing crucial support for integrated land-sea management and risk assessment.

articles.title:
Aqueous
Carbonyl-Amino Aggregation Drives Atmospheric
Nitrogen-Containing Oligomer Formation in China Haze
articles.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-containing organic compounds (NOCs) are ubiquitous in the troposphere and contribute to the reactive nitrogen cycle and aerosol light absorption, yet their formation mechanisms remain unclear, especially in polluted regions. Here, we characterized NOCs in PM2.5 during winter haze in the North China Plain (NCP), with a comparison to those in the Sichuan Basin (ScB). Reduced-nitrogen NOCs (Re-NOCs) accounted for 40% of organics detected in the ESI+ mode, highlighting their importance within atmospheric NOCs. Compared to dry haze (DH) in NCP, high-molecular-weight (HMW, m/z > 250) Re-NOCs in humid haze (HH) were enhanced, which positively correlated with NH4+ and the mass ratio of aqueous-phase secondary organic aerosols to total water-soluble organic aerosols, along with increases in aliphatic chain length and molecular unsaturation, indicating carbonyl-amino-driven oligomerization and cyclization. Aliphatic Re-NOCs dominated the Re-NOCs during HH, together with strong correlations of a typical NOC oligomer (C8H13N3O2) with water-soluble organic nitrogen and HMW Re-NOCs, further suggesting oligomerization as a key formation pathway for NOCs. We found that stronger aerosol acidity and higher temperature favored oligomerization of Re-NOCs compared to cyclization, resulting in enhanced C8H13N3O2 in ScB relative to that in NCP. Our work revealed oligomerization as a critical mechanism shaping the NOC composition, particularly HMW species.

articles.title:
Associations
of PM2.5 and Its Oxidative
Potential with Childhood Allergy-Related Symptoms: A Cross-Sectional
Study in Guangdong Province, China
articles.abstract: Abstract Evidence linking PM2.5 exposure to allergic symptoms remains limited and inconsistent, partly because most studies rely on mass-based metrics alone. We conducted a population-based study among 131,346 children aged 6–18 years in six cities of Guangdong, China, to compare associations of PM2.5 mass concentration, oxidative potential (OP), and chemical components (metals, carbonaceous components, and ions) with rhinitis, rhinoconjunctivitis, and eczema symptoms. OP was assessed using the dithiothreitol assay and expressed as volume-normalized (DTTv) and mass-normalized (DTTm) metrics. PM2.5 mass and OP were generally positively associated with the three allergy-related symptoms. OP, particularly DTTm, provided more consistent and robust evidence of associations across outcomes than PM2.5 mass, supported by lower AIC/BIC values and greater stability in two-pollutant models. Single-component and mixture analyses indicated that multiple PM2.5 constituents contributed to allergy-related symptoms, and OP may partly explain the associations of Co, OC, Cu, and Hg, with the largest estimated indirect proportion reaching 36.2% for OC and rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms through DTTm. These findings suggest that OP captures health-relevant characteristics beyond particle mass and may serve as a complementary exposure indicator for understanding childhood symptoms of allergic diseases.

articles.title:
Regional Impacts
of Unconventional Oil and Gas Operations
on Ozone and Air Toxics
articles.abstract: Abstract Unconventional oil and gas development (UOGD) has expanded over the past three decades and now accounts for most of U.S. oil and natural gas production. Although prior studies link local UOGD activity to health outcomes, they provide limited evidence directly attributing ambient pollutant levels to UOGD emissions. We address this gap by quantifying UOGD impacts on ozone and air toxics using the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model with the Integrated Source Apportionment Method (ISAM), enabling an explicit linkage between UOGD emissions and ambient concentrations. UOGD activities produce substantial local contributions to primary air toxics and continental-scale influences on ozone. Across CONUS, UOGD increases population-weighted annual averages of maximum daily average 8-h (MDA8) ozone, 1-h benzene, 1-h nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and 1-h formaldehyde (HCHO) concentrations by roughly 1 ppb, 1.1 ppt, 0.035 ppb, and 0.03 ppb, respectively. Annual maximum UOGD contributions to MDA8 ozone are about half of those from other anthropogenic sources. ISAM also reveals unexpectedly large UOGD-driven ozone enhancement (up to 4–5 ppb) in the Los Angeles region from Texas emissions, a feature less evident in brute-force sensitivity tests. These findings highlight the need to further examine interstate UOGD influences on nonattainment areas and source-impact quantification methods.

articles.title:
Research
Priorities for a Circular Economy for Plastic
Sustainability in the Caribbean
articles.abstract: Abstract Caribbean countries bear a disproportionate burden of marine plastic pollution because of their small landmass, high population density, and insufficient waste management infrastructure. Many Caribbean nations depend on informal, unmanaged landfills, underscoring an urgent need for more resilient, sustainable systems. This perspective synthesizes existing data to map the region’s plastic waste landscape and leverages regional expertise to identify key research priorities. This work emerged from interdisciplinary international professionals and members of the CEPlaSt (circular economy for plastic sustainability) network. A major barrier to circularity is the lack of reliable data on waste composition and flows, alongside stark infrastructure disparities across the wider Caribbean region. Addressing these gaps through targeted investment and region-specific planning is essential to modernize waste systems, reduce plastic emissions, and advance a sustainable Caribbean plastic circular economy.

articles.title:
Reductive Incorporation
of Technetium-99 in Fe(II)-Doped
Layered Double Hydroxide
articles.abstract: Abstract Technetium-99 is a long-lived, high-yield fission product whose solubility is controlled by redox conditions. Here, to explore targeted effluent treatment approaches, pertechnetate (Tc(VII)O4–) reductive retention as Tc(IV) during coprecipitation of Fe(II)-doped Ni–Al–CO3 layered double hydroxide (LDH) was investigated. During LDH formation via base addition to an acidic Ni2+, Al3+, Fe2+, and Tc(VII)O4– bearing solution, there was essentially complete TcO4– removal at low (9.6 Bq/mL) and high (2.9 kBq/mL) concentrations. Characterization of experiments using X-ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) confirmed that, during base titration, a two-stage process occurred, with Al3+ forming amorphous Al (hydr)oxide between pH 4 and 6 in the first stage, followed by hydrolysis of Fe2+/Ni2+ and formation of LDH particles between pH 6 and 9 in stage two. During the first stage, TcO4– was removed from solution, and XAS confirmed it was reduced to Tc(IV) by Fe(II) associated with the amorphous Al (hydr)oxide, forming hydrous Tc(IV)O2-like chains on the Al (hydr)oxide surface. During the second stage, XAS showed that Tc(IV) was incorporated within the newly formed LDH structure. Overall, these data provide novel insights into the application of LDH formation in Tc sequestration and suggest novel effluent treatment pathways to produce an inorganic solid.

articles.title:
Modeled
Groundwater Decline is Associated with Lower
Arsenic Concentrations in Hanoi
articles.abstract: Abstract Elevated arsenic concentrations in groundwater pose health risks. Geogenic arsenic contamination is driven by biogeochemical mobilization and groundwater dynamics. Intensive pumping can initially exacerbate contamination by drawing arsenic or mobilizing organic matter into aquifers, but over longer time scales may also promote dilution and flushing in some settings. To better understand the mechanisms controlling arsenic concentrations, we examined changes over two decades in Hanoi (Vietnam), a hotspot of geogenic arsenic contamination and groundwater pumping. Arsenic concentrations from 470 wells sampled in the year 2000 were compared with 434 wells sampled in the same area in 2013 and 2023. Median concentrations declined from 14 to 8 μg/L between 2000 and 2023, while mean concentrations and the proportion of high-arsenic wells (>100 μg/L) remained similar. Using hydrochemical and groundwater-level data, CatBoost models combined with SHAP analysis assessed changes in predictor importance. In 2000, arsenic was more strongly associated with redox predictors, whereas groundwater-level predictors became more important in 2023. Within wells used to evaluate groundwater-level change (n = 251), larger decadal declines were associated with lower arsenic concentrations (median = 31 μg/L) than wells without declines (median = 120 μg/L). We hypothesize a decadal mechanism shift, from redox to hydrological controls, particularly driving arsenic declines.

articles.title:
Life-Cycle Burden
Shifting in Solvent-Based Regeneration
of PFOS-Laden Granular Activated Carbon
articles.abstract: Abstract Granular activated carbon (GAC) is widely used to remove perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) from contaminated water, yet its sustainable regeneration remains challenging. Solvent-based regeneration preserves the carbon matrix but may shift environmental burdens toward solvent production, chemical use, energy demand, and downstream waste management. Here we present a life cycle assessment (LCA) of PFOS-laden GAC regeneration using deionized water (GAC-WR) and ethanol (GAC-ER). We identify electricity-driven elution and downstream incineration as the dominant environmental hotspots across 18 midpoint impact categories. Selected chemical-assisted configurations (NaOH-modified water and HCl-modified ethanol) improved regeneration efficiency and reduced environmental impacts under the evaluated conditions by reducing virgin GAC supplementation. An industrial-scale model incorporating equipment upscaling and thermal integration further mitigated laboratory-specific energy overestimation. Compared with the corresponding baseline scenarios using the global electricity mix, hydropower-based electricity reduces global warming potential to 3.30 and 8.26 kg CO2e kg–1 for GAC-WR and GAC-ER, respectively, while increasing life-cycle water consumption to 230% and 266% of the respective baselines. This cross-category burden shift demonstrates that reducing climate impacts does not necessarily reduce the broader life-cycle environmental footprint. Overall, sustainable solvent-based GAC regeneration requires balancing regeneration efficiency, energy supply, chemical inputs, solvent recovery, and management of PFAS-containing wastes.

articles.title:
Micromolar Experiments,
Nanomolar Environments

Nanoplastic Size
Governs the Decoupling of Microbial
Survival from Antibiotic Degradation
articles.abstract: Abstract Nanoplastics (NPs) and antibiotics co-occur in wastewater systems, but how NP size influences antibiotic biodegradation by specialized degraders remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of europium-doped polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs; PS20 and PS100) on sulfadiazine biodegradation by Arthrobacter sp. strain D2. Modified Gompertz modeling revealed two contrasting inhibition regimes. For PS100, inhibition was dominated by lag-phase prolongation, with no detectable sulfadiazine removal over 48 h at a PS100 concentration of 100 mg L–1. In contrast, PS20 reduced the maximum sulfadiazine degradation rate by ∼40% while causing only minor changes in lag time, indicating rate-dominated inhibition. Quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring at a model sulfadiazine-enriched interface showed that PS100 markedly reduced the deposition of NP-pre-exposed cells, whereas PS20 only partially impaired adhesion. Transmission electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy further revealed intracellular accumulation of PS20, whereas PS100 remained predominantly extracellular. Phase-specific physiological measurements and transcriptomics suggested that PS20 induced oxidative-stress responses associated with reduced sulfadiazine biodegradation rates, whereas PS100 elicited dose-dependent transcriptional changes during lag-phase extension. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that nanoplastics impair antibiotic attenuation through distinct size-dependent mechanisms involving interface-associated constraints and intracellular interference, highlighting particle size as a key determinant of antibiotic fate in plastic-contaminated wastewater environments.

articles.title:
Early
Life Ambient
Air Pollution, Sex Steroids and
Neurodevelopment: Target Trial Emulation in a Prospective Cohort
articles.abstract: Abstract Ambient air pollution may impair childhood neurodevelopment, but sensitive windows, mediating pathways, and the neurodevelopmental benefits of air-quality interventions remain unclear. In this prospective birth cohort of 3575 mother–child pairs in Wuhan, China (2014–2019), neurodevelopment at age two was assessed using the Bayley Scales, and cord serum sex steroids were measured in 897 pairs. Associations of air pollution exposure from preconception through the second postnatal year with neurodevelopment at age two and potential sex-steroid mediation were evaluated. Target trial emulation (TTE) was used to estimate neurodevelopmental differences associated with China’s 2013–2017 air-quality intervention. Most air pollutants were inversely associated with neurodevelopment across multiple exposure windows, with associations generally strongest during the first postnatal year. Mediation analyses suggested that androstenedione mediated 5–12% of associations between specific preconception/prenatal air pollutant exposures and Psychomotor Development Index, although inverse-probability-weighted indirect effects were no longer statistically significant. TTE suggested significant neurodevelopmental benefits following the air-quality intervention, with Mental Development Index and Psychomotor Development Index improving by 7.27 and 6.41 points in the later policy-period group, respectively. These findings support more stringent long-term air pollution standards and sustained air-quality interventions to protect child neurodevelopment.

articles.title:
Gas–Liquid
Interface Enhanced Selective Adsorption
of Long-Chain PFAS by Novel Floating Macroporous Resins
articles.abstract: Abstract Long-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in industrial wastewater are a significant source of PFAS contamination. Anion exchange resin (AER) adsorption is an advantageous technology for PFAS removal, but existing AERs suffer from limited selectivity. In this study, our synthesized novel macroporous AERs with asymmetric long-chain amine groups, MP-(12–1–1) and MP-(16–1–1), exhibited a unique floating behavior on the water surface after drying and achieved significantly enhanced PFAS removal from chromium-plating wastewater, with the gas–liquid interface playing a critical role. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the rough surfaces and hydrophobic functional groups of the dry MP-(12–1–1) and MP-(16–1–1) enable them to maintain the Cassie wetting state in water without transitioning to the Wenzel state, thereby forming a stable gas–liquid interface. The gas–liquid interface exhibited adsorption free energies reaching −7.6 to −9.5 kcal/mol for long-chain PFAS, increasing the selectivity of the floating macroporous AERs for various long-chain PFAS by 6–81 times. This provides a new approach for the efficient removal of long-chain PFAS and offers new insights for the design of selective adsorbents based on the gas–liquid interface.

articles.title:
Submicroscale
and
Molecular Insights into Labile Organic
Matter Transformation and Sequestration at Newly Formed Iron Minerals–Water
Interfaces during O2-Mediated Fe(II) Oxidation
articles.abstract: Abstract Abiotic Fe(II) oxidation and subsequent precipitation are key pathways for controlling labile organic matter (OM) dynamics in O2-perturbed subsurface environments, yet the underlying coupling mechanisms remain poorly understood. Herein, OM transformation and sequestration during O2-mediated heterogeneous Fe(II) oxidation were evaluated at neutral pH across various C/Fe ratios. Increasing C/Fe ratios impeded Fe(II) oxidation but enhanced the level of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Despite efficient sequestration, the OM immobilization efficiency varied with C/Fe ratios, with a minor fraction of OM being oxidized by ROS. Higher C/Fe ratios promoted ferrihydrite formation but inhibited its transformation into lepidocrocite, forming mineral-organic composites constituted by Fe–O cores and edge-/corner-sharing Fe–Fe shells. A direct visualization at submicroscale revealed heterogeneous spatial distributions of different organo functional groups on newly formed Fe mineral surfaces, reflecting OM selective immobilization. Newly formed Fe minerals preferentially immobilized high-molecular-weight compounds and those with more oxygenated or highly unsaturated structures, with stronger molecular fractionation at higher C/Fe ratios. Molecular-level analysis revealed that a lower C/Fe ratio promoted the conversion of phenols to quinones, aromatic ring opening, and carboxylation of aromatic substituents but inhibited polymerization of phenolic substances. Collectively, these findings deepen our knowledge of heterogeneous Fe mineral formation coupled with OM sequestration and transformation, advancing our understanding of Fe and C geochemical cycling in oxic soils and sediments.

articles.title: Ocean Acidification Impairs Olfaction in the Large Yellow Croaker, Larimichthys crocea , by Disrupting Sensory Integrity and Neural Processing
articles.abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification (OA) poses a significant threat to marine organisms, yet its effects on fish sensory systems remain poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of elevated pCO2 on olfactory function in the large yellow croaker, Larimichthys crocea. Elevated pCO2 reduced peripheral olfactory sensitivity, as evidenced by suppressed electro-olfactogram responses. This impairment was accompanied by epithelial disorganization, cellular damage, increased apoptosis in the olfactory epithelium, and reduced expression of olfactory neuron markers. In vitro analyses using a selected recombinant L. crocea odorant receptor LORA1–1 showed that acidified pH altered its physicochemical properties and odorant-specific receptor–ligand interaction dynamics. OA also downregulated genes associated with odorant receptor expression, G protein-mediated signaling, calcium-related transduction, and neuronal maturation. Telencephalic responses included altered ion-transport ATPase activities, histopathological abnormalities, oxidative stress, enhanced apoptotic activity, and reduced neuropeptide Y expression. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identified telencephalic molecular changes associated with altered neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction, calcium signaling, glutathione metabolism, apoptosis, mitophagy, MAPK signaling, and olfactory transduction. Our findings suggest that epithelial injury, altered odorant recognition, and disrupted peripheral signaling contribute to OA-induced olfactory impairment in L. crocea, with potential consequences for migration and reproduction that depend on olfactory cues.

articles.title:
Uncovering
the Fate
and Global-Scale Risk-Based Threshold
Contents of Organophosphate Esters in Indoor Environments: A Tiered
Modeling Approach
articles.abstract: Abstract Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are ubiquitous indoors, posing threats to public health. However, limited information on both the permissible levels and environmental behavior makes global regulation challenging. Herein, a closed-loop mechanistic framework, termed the Indoor OPE Source Identification and Exposure Direct Assessment (IOSIEDA) model, tracing the cause-and-effect chain from OPE source contents to health impacts, was developed to forecast indoor OPE emissions and fate, rapidly screen risks, prioritize high-risk OPE-material combinations, and back-calculate risk-based threshold contents (RTCs). Model evaluation via Monte Carlo simulation and a residential case study revealed a total Σ13OPEs influx of ∼2053 μg day–1, predominantly originating from indoor source emissions (99.4%), with 95% loss via air exchange. Notably, the IOSIEDA model back-calculated the RTCs within a risk-based framework built upon the source-specific relationship between OPE contents and emission characteristics, developing health-prevention-oriented thresholds for a set of unregulated OPEs across five types of understudied source materials. Global application across 16 countries provided emissions and an RTC database for indoor OPEs, filling in the missing values for global national thresholds of OPEs in specific source materials. Total residential OPE emissions were estimated at ∼74,500 kg yr–1; Asia constitutes the major emission region, and RTCs exhibit distinct regional disparities across continents.

articles.title: Medium-Entropy LDH-Driven Electronic Coupling of MnO x for Preferential Oxidation of Formaldehyde
articles.abstract: Abstract Preferential oxidation of formaldehyde (HCHO) in natural gas engine exhaust is pivotal to prevent NH3–SCR catalyst deactivation and inhibit highly toxic hydrogen cyanide (HCN) formation. Although manganese-based catalysts exhibit prominent activity for HCHO oxidation, complete mineralization is still hindered by poor electron-transfer efficiency and insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Herein, we fabricate hierarchical medium-entropy LDH nanoflower-anchored MnOx catalysts (MnO2@NiMgAl-MELH) via a facile in situ growth strategy, enabling 100% mineralization of HCHO at room temperature. Structural characterizations and DFT calculations verify that Ni–Mn electronic coupling optimizes the electronic structure, facilitates charge transfer, reduces oxygen vacancy formation energy, and boosts O2 and H2O activation to generate abundant ROS (O2–, O22–, and surface −OH). Furthermore, in situ DRIFTS confirms that ROS synergistically accelerate HCHO and formate intermediate oxidation, achieving complete mineralization of HCHO. This work develops a low-cost and high-performance catalyst for HCHO preferential oxidation and offers a broadly applicable strategy for air pollutant purification.

articles.title:
Voltage-Dependent
Metabolic Shifts Regulate the Fouling
Behavior of the Anaerobic-Anodic Membrane
articles.abstract: Abstract Fouling remains the key barrier to durable membrane operation, against which electrochemical processes offer a promising fouling control strategy. However, the performance of an anodic membrane under anaerobic conditions exhibits significant instability, the mechanism of which remains unclear and represents a critical knowledge gap. This study systematically investigated the response of membrane fouling evolution to gradient electric fields within anodic membranes. A distinct threshold behavior of electric field strength on membrane fouling was observed, with a system-dependent threshold occurring between 0.7 and 1.0 V. Following an initial fouling layer, subthreshold fields (≤0.7 V) exacerbated fouling accumulation, whereas supra-threshold fields (≥1.0 V) slowed down membrane fouling development. Comprehensive analysis revealed that surpassing critical field strength enhanced anodic electron-accepting capacity, likely facilitating microbial extracellular electron release and alleviating reductive pressure. This triggered a nonlinear, threshold-dependent metabolic switch from biosynthesis-dominated to catabolism-enhanced pathways, coupled with quorum quenching that inhibited biofilm maturation. These synergistic transitions underpinned the fouling reversal. This work advances the understanding of anaerobic-anodic membrane fouling from an empirical observation into a threshold-governed electrochemical–microbial switching process, thereby providing the scientific foundation for harnessing this interplay to achieve durable and efficient operation in anaerobic wastewater treatment and resource recovery systems.
